findings.issue_text: [BUG] The replacement changes the light-theme value from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), so dark-light-choose's first branch no longer matches the original light appearance. In light themes the small-post reply-to/user link color jumps from a near-primary (30% lightness) to a much dimmer 70% lightness gray, an unintended visible regression on the light theme, not just a dark-theme fix.

[BUG] .custom-message-length replaces scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), ...), changing the light-theme value from 70% to 30% lightness. Light themes render the composer character-count hint much darker than before, an unintended light-theme change bundled into a dark-theme PR.

[BUG] The .topic-links h3 rule replaces scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...), changing the light-theme value from 20% to 50% lightness. Light themes show the embedded-topic link heading noticeably lighter than the pre-change value, an unintended regression in a dark-theme-only PR.

[BUG] .user-main .about .details .name replaces scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...), changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50%. The user profile display-name color lightens from 30% to 50% lightness in light themes, an unintended visual change beyond the stated dark-theme scope.

[BUG] .user-main .about .details .name replaces scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...), changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50%. Mobile light themes show the profile display-name in a lighter shade than before, an unintended light-theme regression.

[BUG] The light-mode value of .custom-message-length is silently changed from 70% to 30% lightness instead of only wrapping in dark-light-choose, violating the PR's stated scope (light themes unchanged). Light-theme users see the custom-message-length hint jump from a faint to a near-full-contrast color; the diff contradicts its own acceptance criterion ('scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes' — i.e., a dark-only fix).

[BUG] The h3 rule's light-mode value is silently changed from 20% to 50% lightness while the diff only claims to add a dark-theme branch. Light-theme topic-list headers (suggested topics) lose their intended near-#primary emphasis and render at the muted 50% tone, an unadvertised visual regression in every light color scheme.

[BUG] The .name rule's light-mode value is silently changed from 30% to 50% lightness, and the sibling .username rule in common/base/user.scss keeps 30%, so the same name/username pair now renders inconsistently in light themes. Light-theme user cards show .name at 50% while .username stays at 30%, a visible mismatch introduced by a diff that claims to touch only dark-theme colors.

[BUG] The mobile .name rule's light-mode value is silently changed from 30% to 50% lightness, diverging from the untouched .username (30%) and contradicting the dark-only scope of the PR. Light-theme mobile user cards show the display name dimmer than the username next to it, an unadvertised light-mode regression.

[ADVISORY] The diff's conversion pass is incomplete on this same file/selector: the adjacent .wmd-input rule still uses color: darken($primary, 40%), a hard darken() that is broken on dark themes, left untouched by a PR dedicated to fixing dark-theme colors on this exact path. Dark-theme composers get text computed from darkening an already-dark $primary, the same class of bug this PR exists to fix, on the very element the PR edits three lines above.

[BUG] The mobile badge-glyph h3 is converted with lightness 50%/50%, while the identical desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss h3) is converted 20%/80%, breaking the mirror-inversion convention (dark-theme secondary lightness = 100 − primary lightness) used everywhere else in this PR. On dark themes the mobile badge heading renders at a visibly different shade than desktop for the same element; the value is not traceable to the conversion rule the rest of the diff follows, so it reads as a copy-paste slip rather than an intended design choice.

[BUG] .name is converted from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%), collapsing it to the exact same color as the adjacent .title rule (also 50%/50%) instead of the 70% the inversion rule dictates — the same drift appears in mobile/user.scss:494. On dark themes the user's name and title render identically, erasing the visual hierarchy between the two lines; the 30% source value was deliberately preserved in common/base/user.scss (.name converted to 70%) but was silently changed to 50% here, so the two copies of the same rule now diverge.

[BUG] The .replies-to section's link color silently changed the light-mode value from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) while adding the dark-light-choose wrapper, altering light-theme rendering instead of only adding a dark-mode value Users of the light theme see reply-to links rendered at 70% lightness instead of 30% — a drastically dimmer (in dark-on-light themes, washed-out) color not intended by this dark-theme PR

[BUG] The .name color's light-mode value was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while adding the dark-light-choose wrapper Light-theme users see the profile name dimmed to the 50% tone; the change also desynchronizes this selector from the identical .name rule in common/base/user.scss (which stays at 30%), so desktop and common renderings diverge

[BUG] The mobile .name color's light-mode value was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while adding the dark-light-choose wrapper Mobile light-theme users see the profile name at 50% instead of 30% lightness, diverging from the desktop/common value of 30% for the same element

[BUG] The .custom-message-length color's light-mode value was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) while adding the dark-light-choose wrapper (the desktop rule keeps 70%/30% pairing, so the two now disagree) Mobile light-theme users see the custom-message-length hint at 30% lightness instead of 70%, and mobile vs desktop render the same hint with mismatched colors

[BUG] The topic-map h3 color's light-mode value was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while adding the dark-light-choose wrapper (desktop/topic-post.scss h3 keeps 20%) Mobile light-theme users see the topic-map heading at 50% instead of 20% lightness, and mobile diverges from the desktop heading color for the same component

[BUG] The light-theme value was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 70%, so the diff does not preserve the original intent of only fixing dark themes. Light-theme users see the 'in reply to' username/date links rendered at lightness 70% instead of 30% — a visible contrast regression introduced without being part of the stated PR goal; the change is buried in a mechanical dark-theme sweep and was never explicitly accepted.

[BUG] The .name color's light-theme value was changed from $lightness: 30% to $lightness: 50% while wrapping in dark-light-choose, drifting from the PR's stated scope. Light-theme user profile names lose contrast (30% → 50% lightness), a visible change to light themes that the PR title and intent ('$lightness must use $secondary for dark themes') does not authorize; the desktop and mobile copies of this same rule drift identically, indicating an unreviewed mechanical edit.

[BUG] Same silent light-theme value change as desktop/user.scss: .name moves from $lightness: 30% to $lightness: 50%. Mobile light-theme user names are dimmed relative to the previous shipped appearance without any stated intent or review acceptance.

[BUG] The h3 color's light-theme value was changed from $lightness: 20% to $lightness: 50%, contradicting the PR's dark-theme-only intent. Mobile light-theme link-modal/topic-preview headings lose their emphasized dark styling (20% → 50% lightness), a visible regression on light themes hidden inside a mechanical find-and-replace.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length light-theme value was changed from $lightness: 70% to $lightness: 30%. Light-theme modals render the character-count hint much darker than before (70% → 30%), making a deliberately subtle hint visually prominent — an unrequested light-theme change bundled into the dark-theme fix.

[BUG] The #draft-status light-theme value was changed from $lightness: 75% to $lightness: 25%. The draft-status indicator on mobile light themes jumps from a faint 75%-lightness gray to a near-primary 25% color, an unrequested visual change to light themes smuggled into the dark-theme sweep.

[ADVISORY] The diff establishes an unstated invariant (dark lightness = 100% − light lightness against $secondary) maintained by hand across ~60 call sites with no single source of truth. Every future color edit requires manually keeping the two branches complementary; the six drift sites in this very diff (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/compose.scss:51) demonstrate the failure mode is already active — the next contributor editing one branch will silently desynchronize the other.

[ADVISORY] The .name light-theme value changes from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50% while the diff's stated purpose is only dark-theme fixing, so light themes silently shift contrast. Users of light themes get a dimmer username than before; the change rides in unflagged inside a dark-theme PR and no reviewer is prompted to confirm it is intentional.

[ADVISORY] h3 light-theme value changes from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to 50% in a PR whose scope is dark-theme color fixes. Light-theme mobile user-card headings become noticeably dimmer without an explicit callout, and the paired h4 stays at 50% so the prior 20%/50% hierarchy between h3 and h4 collapses to identical values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff establishes an unstated invariant (dark lightness = 100% − light lightness against $secondary) maintained by hand across ~60 call sites with no single source of truth. adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces many `scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%)` uses with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, X%), scale-color($secondary, Y%))`, and in most cases `Y` is the hand-maintained complement of `X` (e.g., 40/60, 25/75, 70/30, 45/55). This supports the finding that the PR introduces/relies on a repeated, implicit mapping across many call sites without a single source of truth, creating maintainability/drift risk. It’s not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone, but it is a specific, diff-grounded review concern.
